question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, which of the following states has the largest percentage of poor people?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023** (MPI) is based on indicators including health, education, and standard of living.
 
• According to the 2023 MPI, **Jharkhand has the largest percentage of poor people** in India, accounting for approximately 29.4% of its population being multidimensionally poor.
 
• The MPI measures poverty using 12 indicators across three dimensions: **health, education, and living standards**.
 
• Jharkhand has historically faced challenges such as low literacy rates, poor healthcare facilities, and lack of infrastructure development, contributing to its higher poverty index.
 
• The state government is actively working to address poverty through schemes like **Jharkhand State Livelihood Promotion Society (JSLPS)** and initiatives in rural development, skill training, and health improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya**

 
 
• While Meghalaya has a significant percentage of poverty, it has performed better in certain dimensions of MPI such as health and education compared to Jharkhand.
 
• Meghalaya has undertaken initiatives to improve literacy rates and healthcare accessibility, including programs like the **Meghalaya Health Insurance Scheme**.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh**
 
 
• Uttar Pradesh has a large population base, and poverty alleviation remains a challenge despite numerous development schemes.
 
• The state has implemented programs like **Mission Shakti** and **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana** to improve living standards and women's empowerment.
 
• While poverty levels are high, they are lower than Jharkhand's in terms of multidimensional poverty.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**
 
 
• Andhra Pradesh has shown significant improvement in poverty reduction due to developmental initiatives such as **Navaratnalu**, focusing on healthcare, housing, and education.
 
• The state has a relatively better MPI ranking compared to Jharkhand due to its focused approach towards improving infrastructure and social welfare.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index**

 
 
• The MPI is prepared by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• The index is based on the findings of the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5)**.
 
• It is a tool to assess poverty beyond income, focusing on multiple indicators like nutrition, child mortality, school attendance, sanitation, and access to drinking water.
